labels.name: area:configuration
labels.description: Relates to configuration options

labels.name: kind:enhancement
labels.description: Indicates a new feature request, imrovement, or extension

labels.name: ide:vscode
labels.description: Relates specifically to VS Code extension

items.body:
### Validations

- [X] I believe this is a way to improve. I'll try to join the [Continue Discord](https://discord.gg/NWtdYexhMs) for questions
- [X] I'm not able to find an [open issue](https://github.com/continuedev/continue/issues?q=is%3Aopen+is%3Aissue+label%3Aenhancement) that requests the same enhancement

### Problem

I don't like that all the API keys are stored in plain text in a JSON file at the user root. I know that this is required for VSCode, and every other plugin that uses API has to do this. It just doesn't sit right with me. 

### Solution

At the very least, put a .gitignore at the root of .continue to make sure config.json doesn't get indexed. It may also be possible to write external scripts that encrypt the config.json if the user wants to be security-conscious.

items.title: Feature Request: Automatic File Creation/Editing

labels.name: area:inline-edit
labels.description: Relates to the auto refactor feature

labels.name: kind:enhancement
labels.description: Indicates a new feature request, imrovement, or extension

items.body:
### Validations

- [x] I believe this is a way to improve. I'll try to join the [Continue Discord](https://discord.gg/NWtdYexhMs) for questions
- [x] I'm not able to find an [open issue](https://github.com/continuedev/continue/issues?q=is%3Aopen+is%3Aissue+label%3Aenhancement) that requests the same enhancement

### Problem

Currently, when the Continue extension provides suggestions that involve creating a new file or editing an existing one, users have to manually create the file or navigate to it to apply the changes. This can be time-consuming and disrupts the workflow.

**Proposed Solution:**
The extension should automatically create or edit files when applying suggestions. For example:
- If a suggestion involves creating a new file, the extension should create the file and apply the changes.
- If a suggestion involves editing an existing file, the extension should open the file (if not already open) and apply the changes.

**Benefits:**
- Improved productivity by reducing manual steps.
- Seamless integration into the development workflow.

**Additional Context:**
This feature would be particularly useful when working with large projects or when the extension suggests multiple file changes at once.

### Solution

items.title: Default Linux Config Directory Should Be .config/continue

labels.name: area:configuration
labels.description: Relates to configuration options

labels.name: kind:enhancement
labels.description: Indicates a new feature request, imrovement, or extension

labels.name: os:linux
labels.description: Happening specifically on Linux

items.body:
### Validations

- [x] I believe this is a way to improve. I'll try to join the [Continue Discord](https://discord.gg/NWtdYexhMs) for questions
- [x] I'm not able to find an [open issue](https://github.com/continuedev/continue/issues?q=is%3Aopen+is%3Aissue+label%3Aenhancement) that requests the same enhancement

### Problem

In most Linux distros, we expect user config to go into `.config/`.

If present, it should also respect `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`.

Most of us don't want our home directories cluttered with config files.

### Solution

Change the default config location.
